transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I don’t know… I just can’t really make myself do anything anymore. I mostly sit in my room, wear the same clothes. I stopped doing stuff I used to do, like knitting or writing in my journal or going for walks. When my mom asks what’s wrong, I just… don’t really have the energy to answer.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I don’t know… not exactly. I just feel kind of empty, I guess. Not really sad all the time.
Do you still enjoy anything?
Not really. I mean… I used to like knitting, and writing in my journal, going for walks. Now I just kind of sit in my room. I don’t really start anything.
Do you ever feel detached from yourself, like you’re watching yourself from outside your body?
I don’t think so… not like outside my body. I just feel kind of blank sometimes.
Have you ever heard voices when no one was there?
I… I’m not really sure. I don’t think so. Not like a real voice, maybe… I don’t know.
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt like this for weeks or longer?
I don’t know… I can’t really remember another time like this. Maybe I’ve had bad stretches, but not… I’m not sure.
Have you ever believed something was true that other people said could not be true?

Yeah… I guess. Since I was in those college classes, I started noticing stuff in the school portal, and emails, like the wording was changed a little. Same with comments from the clinic practicum people. It felt like they were marking me as someone they didn’t want in healthcare. My mom says they’re just normal messages, but… it doesn’t feel that way to me.
Do you believe for certain that those messages were deliberately changed to single you out?

Yeah… I mean, I know how it sounds, but yes. The wording was changed on purpose. In the portal, in the emails, even the practicum comments… it felt like they were signaling that I shouldn’t be in healthcare. My mom says it’s normal stuff, but I don’t think it is.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being controlled by someone or something outside you?

Not like… controlling my thoughts exactly. It’s more that the school portal and the clinic people were using little wording changes, like in emails and comments, to single me out. Like they were marking me as someone they didn’t want in healthcare. My mom says they’re normal messages, but I don’t think so.
For most of the day, nearly every day, have you been feeling depressed?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say most of the day every day. I get down sometimes, but I’m not really sure.
For longer than one month, have you believed that the school portal, emails, or practicum comments were deliberately changed to single you out?
Yeah… longer than a month. It’s been pretty fixed like that for maybe two months now.
Have you heard voices talking to you when no one else was there?
No… I don’t think so. Not voices talking to me, at least.
Has there been a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly all day, almost every day?
I’m not really sure. I’ve felt low sometimes, but I don’t know if it was like… nearly all day for two weeks.
Before the school email and portal concerns started, had you already begun losing motivation and interest in things like knitting, writing, or going for walks?

Yeah… I think that started before. I just kind of stopped doing things. I stay in my room a lot, same clothes sometimes, and I don’t really knit or write or go on walks anymore. When my mom asks, I don’t really know what to say.
Has your face or voice felt less expressive than usual to other people?
I guess… yeah. My mom says I sound kind of flat sometimes. I don’t really notice my face, but I don’t have much energy to talk or react. I mostly just sit in my room and… don’t do much.
At times when you were not feeling low or empty, did you still believe the school messages were being deliberately changed to single you out?

Yeah… even when I wasn’t feeling especially low, I still thought that. The school portal and the practicum people… it was like the wording in emails or assignment comments would change just enough to show they were singling me out, like they didn’t want me in healthcare. My mom says they’re just normal messages, but it doesn’t feel that way to me.
Have other people had trouble following what you say because your speech seemed hard to understand or jumped from topic to topic?
I’m not sure. I don’t really notice how I sound. Sometimes people ask me to repeat myself, but… I don’t know if it’s because I’m jumping around or just not explaining it right.
Have these problems with motivation and doing less than usual been going on for at least six months?
Yeah… definitely more than six months. It’s kind of been since I started the community college program, so… about two years, maybe a little over. Two years and a couple months.
Compared with before all this started, have you been doing worse at school or work?

Yeah… I’m doing worse. I kind of had to stop moving forward in the certificate program. I can’t really handle the practicum part, and the clinic office job I was trying to work toward… I’m not really able to plan for that now.
Has there ever been a time that lasted at least two weeks when you felt sad or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?
I don’t know… I mean, I get down sometimes, but I’m not sure if it was like that for two weeks straight, most of the day.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with residual schizophrenia: there is a persistent delusional belief of being singled out through altered school/clinic communications, along with prominent negative symptoms (marked avolition, anhedonia, social withdrawal, reduced self-care, and flat affect) lasting well over 6 months with clear functional decline. Depressive syndromes were not clearly established by duration or pervasiveness, and the psychotic belief persists even outside low mood states, arguing against a primary depressive disorder. Delusional disorder was considered because of the fixed persecutory idea, but the substantial negative symptoms and deterioration in functioning over a prolonged period favor schizophrenia-spectrum illness.
